page: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v6 is an ARM-based server instance powered by a Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores running at 3.4 GHz with 1.0 thread per core, backed by 128.0 GB of RAM. The CPU includes a 128 MB L3 cache and supports AES cryptography, though it lacks AVX and AMX vector extensions. Local storage is provided via a bundled 1890 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier memory performance, with uncached read-only large block memory bandwidth reaching 448.6 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 188.32 GB/sec. Passmark database operations and memory scores also rank in the top 10%. Multi-core processing is strong, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 20037.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 66288.64. However, single-core metrics, such as the Geekbench single-core score of 1686.0, fall into the average tier. Large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with prompt processing for a 70B model registering in the bottom 10% at 4.65 tokens/sec.

The ARM64 architecture provides high resource density and excellent memory bandwidth efficiency relative to its hardware profile. The lack of hyperthreading and dedicated physical core allocation ensures predictable execution. This makes the instance highly efficient for database operations, Redis caching, static web serving, and software compilation. It is less optimal for workloads requiring specialized x86 vector instructions or heavy large-language model inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v6 is an ARM-based general-purpose server instance featuring 32 dedicated physical cores on a 3.4 GHz Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. Equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 1890 GB NVMe SSD, it delivers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Benchmark results highlight top-tier memory performance, with uncached read memory bandwidth reaching 448.6 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 188.32 GB/sec, alongside top-tier Passmark database operations. Multi-core capabilities are strong, supported by a Geekbench multi-core score of 20037.0, though single-core performance and large LLM inference speeds remain average to poor. Lacking AVX and AMX vector extensions, this instance is optimized for database workloads, Redis caching, static web serving, and software compilation rather than vector-heavy compute or large-scale AI inference.
